name: BloodHound Community Edition (CE) - Modern AD Attack Path Mapping
description: BloodHound Community Edition (CE) is the modern rewrite of BloodHound with a PostgreSQL backend (replacing Neo4j), REST API, improved UI, and built-in attack path analysis. It identifies AD/AzureAD privilege escalation paths, ACL abuse chains, and Tier-0 asset exposure. SharpHound or BloodHound.py collectors feed data into it.
notes:
=== INSTALL BLOODHOUND CE ===
  curl -L https://ghst.ly/getbhce | docker compose -f - up
  # Access at http://localhost:8080
  # Default creds shown in console output on first run

=== COLLECT DATA ===
  # SharpHound (Windows):
  SharpHound.exe -c All --zipfilename bh_data.zip
  # Or PowerShell:
  Invoke-BloodHound -CollectionMethod All -ZipFileName bh_data.zip

  # BloodHound.py (Linux):
  bloodhound-python -u <user> -p <pass> -d <domain> -dc <dc_ip> -c All

=== UPLOAD DATA ===
  # Upload ZIP via the CE web UI or API

=== KEY QUERIES ===
  # Built-in attack paths:
  - Shortest path to Domain Admin
  - Kerberoastable users with admin paths
  - Unconstrained delegation systems
  - ADCS attack paths
  - Azure/EntraID privilege escalation

=== API USAGE ===
  # BloodHound CE exposes a REST API:
  curl http://localhost:8080/api/v2/available-domains -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

=== LEGACY vs CE ===
  Legacy: Neo4j + Electron app, Cypher queries
  CE: PostgreSQL + Web UI, REST API, built-in analysis
  Both use the same SharpHound/bloodhound-python collectors

recommended.note: bloodhound-python is the Linux collector for BloodHound CE.
Legacy BloodHound with Neo4j for custom Cypher queries.

defense.why_it_works: BloodHound maps Active Directory relationships (group memberships, ACLs, sessions, delegations) into a graph database and finds attack paths that are invisible to manual enumeration. It reveals multi-hop privilege escalation chains.
defense.prerequisites: Domain user credentials for data collection; Docker for BloodHound CE server.
defense.impact: Reveals all privilege escalation paths in the domain; identifies Tier-0 exposure and ACL abuse chains.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.002] SharpHound collection generates high-volume LDAP queries; unusual SamAccountName and groupMembership enumeration.
defense.artifacts: LDAP query logs showing full AD enumeration; SharpHound ZIP files; network connections to all domain controllers.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText="*SharpHound*" OR ScriptBlockText="*Invoke-BloodHound*"
| table _time, ComputerName, UserName, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4104
| where CommandLine has "SharpHound" or CommandLine has "BloodHound"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, CommandLine
defense.prevention: Detect and block SharpHound execution via AMSI/EDR; monitor for mass LDAP enumeration; restrict unnecessary LDAP read access; use honeypot accounts that trigger on enumeration.

detections.name: SharpHound/BloodHound collection activity
detections.logic:
union
(SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4104 | where CommandLine has_any ("SharpHound", "Invoke-BloodHound")),
(DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName =~ "SharpHound.exe" or ProcessCommandLine has "SharpHound")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Authorized red team or security assessment activities
detections.tuning: Alert on any detection; whitelist only during authorized engagements
